sanskrit: chāyāṃ svaputrasadṛśīṃ sarvato 'napagāṃ sadā drakṣyase tvaṃ ca loke 'smin matprasādān mahāmune
english: A shadow resembling your own son, never departing from you on any side, you shall behold always in this world, O great sage, by my grace.

sanskrit: so 'nunīto bhagavatā svayaṃ rudreṇa bhārata chāyāṃ paśyan samāvṛttaḥ sa muniḥ parayā mudā
english: Thus consoled by the blessed Lord Rudra himself, O descendant of Bharata, that sage, beholding the shadow, returned home with the highest joy.

sanskrit: iti janma gatiś caiva śukasya bharatarṣabha vistareṇa mayākhyātaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: Thus the birth and the destiny of Śuka, O bull of the Bharatas, have I recounted to you in full, even as you questioned me.

sanskrit: etad ācaṣṭa me rājan devarṣir nāradaḥ purā vyāsaś caiva mahāyogī saṃjalpeṣu pade pade
english: This the divine seer Nārada related to me of old, O king, and so too the great yogin Vyāsa, again and again in our converse.

sanskrit: itihāsam imaṃ puṇyaṃ mokṣadharmārthasaṃhitam dhārayed yaḥ śamaparaḥ sa gacchet paramāṃ gatim
english: Whoever, devoted to inward peace, holds fast to this holy narrative, fraught with the law and aim of liberation, attains the supreme goal.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca gṛhastho brahmacārī vā vānaprastho 'tha bhikṣukaḥ ya icchet siddhim āsthātuṃ devatāṃ kāṃ yajeta saḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: A householder, a student of sacred lore, a forest-dweller, or a mendicant — whoever should desire to attain perfection, which deity is he to worship?

sanskrit: kuto hy asya dhruvaḥ svargaḥ kuto niḥśreyasaṃ param vidhinā kena juhuyād daivaṃ pitryaṃ tathaiva ca
english: Whence comes to him an enduring heaven, whence the highest beatitude? By what rite should he make oblation to the gods and likewise to the fathers?

sanskrit: muktaś ca kāṃ gatiṃ gacchen mokṣaś caiva kimātmakaḥ svargataś caiva kiṃ kuryād yena na cyavate divaḥ
english: To what goal does the liberated man go, and of what nature is liberation itself? And one who has reached heaven, what should he do so that he does not fall from that realm?

sanskrit: devatānāṃ ca ko devaḥ pitṝṇāṃ ca tathā pitā tasmāt parataraṃ yac ca tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Who is the god of the gods, and who the father of the fathers, and what is higher still than these — that tell me, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca gūḍhaṃ māṃ praśnavit praśnaṃ pṛcchase tvam ihānagha na hy eṣa tarkayā śakyo vaktuṃ varṣaśatair api
english: Bhīṣma said: A hidden question you put to me here, O sinless one, you who know how to question; for this cannot be answered by reasoning, not even in a hundred years.

sanskrit: ṛte devaprasādād vā rājañ jñānāgamena vā gahanaṃ hy etad ākhyānaṃ vyākhyātavyaṃ tavārihan
english: Save by the grace of the god, O king, or by the coming of true knowledge — for profound is this teaching that must be expounded to you, O scourge of foes.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nāradasya ca saṃvādam ṛṣer nārāyaṇasya ca
english: On this point too they relate an ancient tale: the colloquy of Nārada and of the seer Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇo hi viśvātmā caturmūrtiḥ sanātanaḥ dharmātmajaḥ saṃbabhūva pitaivaṃ me 'bhyabhāṣata
english: For Nārāyaṇa, the Self of all, fourfold in form, eternal, came to be born as the son of Dharma — thus did my father declare to me.

sanskrit: kṛte yuge mahārāja purā svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare naro nārāyaṇaś caiva hariḥ kṛṣṇas tathaiva ca
english: In the Kṛta age of old, O great king, in the epoch of Svāyaṃbhuva, there were Nara and Nārāyaṇa, and Hari and Kṛṣṇa as well.

sanskrit: tebhyo nārāyaṇanarau tapas tepatur avyayau badaryāśramam āsādya śakaṭe kanakāmaye
english: Of these, the imperishable Nara and Nārāyaṇa practised austerity, having reached the hermitage of Badarī, seated in a chariot wrought of gold.

sanskrit: aṣṭacakraṃ hi tad yānaṃ bhūtayuktaṃ manoramam tatrādyau lokanāthau tau kṛśau dhamanisaṃtatau
english: Eight-wheeled was that conveyance, yoked with living powers and delightful; there those two primordial lords of the worlds sat, lean, their veins standing forth.

sanskrit: tapasā tejasā caiva durnirīkṣau surair api yasya prasādaṃ kurvāte sa devau draṣṭum arhati
english: By their austerity and their splendour hard to look upon even for the gods — he upon whom the two bestow their grace is fit to behold those divinities.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ tayor anumate hṛdi hṛcchayacoditaḥ mahāmeror gireḥ śṛṅgāt pracyuto gandhamādanam
english: Surely by their leave, urged in his heart by the longing that dwells in the heart, Nārada slipped from the peak of the great mountain Meru toward Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: nāradaḥ sumahad bhūtaṃ lokān sarvān acīcarat taṃ deśam agamad rājan badaryāśramam āśugaḥ
english: Nārada, that mighty being, who had ranged through all the worlds, came swift as the wind to that region, O king, the hermitage of Badarī.

sanskrit: tayor āhnikavelāyāṃ tasya kautūhalaṃ tv abhūt idaṃ tad āspadaṃ kṛtsnaṃ yasmiṃl lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: At the hour of their daily rites a wonder arose in him: This is the whole foundation upon which the worlds are established.

sanskrit: sadevāsuragandharvāḥ sarṣikiṃnaralelihāḥ ekā mūrtir iyaṃ pūrvaṃ jātā bhūyaś caturvidhā
english: With its gods, asuras, and gandharvas, with its seers, kiṃnaras, and serpents — this was at first a single form, then became fourfold.

sanskrit: dharmasya kulasaṃtāno mahān ebhir vivardhitaḥ aho hy anugṛhīto 'dya dharma ebhiḥ surair iha naranārāyaṇābhyāṃ ca kṛṣṇena hariṇā tathā
english: The great lineage of Dharma has been increased by these. Ah, today is Dharma graced here by these gods — by Nara and Nārāyaṇa, and by Kṛṣṇa and Hari likewise.

sanskrit: tatra kṛṣṇo hariś caiva kasmiṃś cit kāraṇāntare sthitau dharmottarau hy etau tathā tapasi dhiṣṭhitau
english: There Kṛṣṇa and Hari, abiding upon some other occasion, intent upon righteousness, were thus established in austerity.

sanskrit: etau hi paramaṃ dhāma kānayor āhnikakriyā pitarau sarvabhūtānāṃ daivataṃ ca yaśasvinau kāṃ devatāṃ nu yajataḥ pitṝn vā kān mahāmatī
english: These two are the supreme abode — what then is their daily rite? Fathers of all beings, themselves divine and glorious, what deity do these two of great mind worship, or what fathers?

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya manasā bhaktyā nārāyaṇasya ha sahasā prādurabhavat samīpe devayos tadā
english: Reflecting thus in his mind, through devotion to Nārāyaṇa, he at once appeared near the two gods at that moment.

sanskrit: kṛte daive ca pitrye ca tatas tābhyāṃ nirīkṣitaḥ pūjitaś caiva vidhinā yathāproktena śāstrataḥ
english: When the rites to the gods and to the fathers had been performed, he was then beheld by the two and honoured with the rite as prescribed by scripture.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryam apūrvaṃ vidhivistaram upopaviṣṭaḥ suprīto nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Beholding that great marvel, that unprecedented fullness of ritual, the blessed seer Nārada, well pleased, took his seat beside them.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇaṃ saṃnirīkṣya prasannenāntarātmanā namaskṛtvā mahādevam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Gazing upon Nārāyaṇa with a serene inmost soul, having bowed to the Great God, he spoke these words.

sanskrit: vedeṣu sapurāṇeṣu sāṅgopāṅgeṣu gīyase tvam ajaḥ śāśvato dhātā mato 'mṛtam anuttamam pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhūtabhavyaṃ tvayi sarvam idaṃ jagat
english: In the Vedas together with the Purāṇas, with their limbs and sub-limbs, you are sung: you the unborn, the eternal, the ordainer, held to be the imperishable beyond which there is none higher; in you stands all that has been and is to be, this whole world.

sanskrit: catvāro hy āśramā deva sarve gārhasthyamūlakāḥ yajante tvām aharahar nānāmūrtisamāsthitam
english: The four orders of life, O god, all rooted in the householder's state, worship you day after day, you who abide established in manifold forms.

sanskrit: pitā mātā ca sarvasya jagataḥ śāśvato guruḥ kaṃ tv adya yajase devaṃ pitaraṃ kaṃ na vidmahe
english: Father and mother and eternal teacher of the whole world are you — yet whom do you today worship as god, and whom as father? We do not know.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca avācyam etad vaktavyam ātmaguhyaṃ sanātanam tava bhaktimato brahman vakṣyāmi tu yathātatham
english: The blessed Lord said: This is the unspeakable that must be spoken, the eternal mystery of the Self; yet to you who are full of devotion, O brāhmaṇa, I shall declare it as it truly is.

sanskrit: yat tat sūkṣmam avijñeyam avyaktam acalaṃ dhruvam indriyair indriyārthaiś ca sarvabhūtaiś ca varjitam
english: That which is subtle, unknowable, unmanifest, unmoving, abiding, devoid of the senses and the objects of the senses and of all elements —

sanskrit: sa hy antarātmā bhūtānāṃ kṣetrajñaś ceti kathyate triguṇavyatirikto 'sau puruṣaś ceti kalpitaḥ tasmād avyaktam utpannaṃ triguṇaṃ dvijasattama
english: That is the inner Self of beings, and it is called the Knower of the Field; transcending the three strands, it is conceived as the Spirit. From it arose the Unmanifest, made of the three strands, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: avyaktā vyaktabhāvasthā yā sā prakṛtir avyayā tāṃ yonim āvayor viddhi yo 'sau sadasadātmakaḥ āvābhyāṃ pūjyate 'sau hi daive pitrye ca kalpite
english: The Unmanifest, abiding in the state of the manifest, that is imperishable Nature; know her to be the womb of us two — and that which is of the nature of being and non-being is worshipped by us both in the rites ordained for gods and for fathers.

sanskrit: nāsti tasmāt paro 'nyo hi pitā devo 'tha vā dvijaḥ ātmā hi nau sa vijñeyas tatas taṃ pūjayāvahe
english: There is no other higher than That, no father or god, O brāhmaṇa; that is to be known as the very Self of us two, and therefore we worship it.

sanskrit: tenaiṣā prathitā brahman maryādā lokabhāvinī daivaṃ pitryaṃ ca kartavyam iti tasyānuśāsanam
english: By That, O brāhmaṇa, has this bound been laid down, that shapes the worlds: the rite to the gods and to the fathers is to be performed — such is its ordinance.

sanskrit: brahmā sthāṇur manur dakṣo bhṛgur dharmas tapo damaḥ marīcir aṅgirātriś ca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ
english: Brahmā, Sthāṇu, Manu, Dakṣa, Bhṛgu, Dharma, Tapas, Dama, Marīci, Aṅgiras and Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaḥ parameṣṭhī ca vivasvān soma eva ca kardamaś cāpi yaḥ proktaḥ krodho vikrīta eva ca
english: Vasiṣṭha and Parameṣṭhin, Vivasvat and Soma, he who is called Kardama, and Krodha and Vikrīta —

sanskrit: ekaviṃśatir utpannās te prajāpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ tasya devasya maryādāṃ pūjayanti sanātanīm
english: twenty-one in number arose, and these are remembered as the Lords of Creatures; they honour the eternal bound of that god.

sanskrit: daivaṃ pitryaṃ ca satataṃ tasya vijñāya tattvataḥ ātmaprāptāni ca tato jānanti dvijasattamāḥ
english: Knowing truly the rites to the gods and to the fathers as ever belonging to That, the best of the twice-born thereby come to know the things that are attained within the Self.

sanskrit: svargasthā api ye ke cit taṃ namasyanti dehinaḥ te tatprasādād gacchanti tenādiṣṭaphalāṃ gatim
english: Whatever embodied beings, even those dwelling in heaven, bow down to That, they by its grace go to the goal whose fruit has been appointed by it.

sanskrit: ye hīnāḥ saptadaśabhir guṇaiḥ karmabhir eva ca kalāḥ pañcadaśa tyaktvā te muktā iti niścayaḥ
english: Those who are freed of the seventeen attributes and of works as well, and have cast off the fifteen parts — these, it is determined, are the liberated.

sanskrit: muktānāṃ tu gatir brahman kṣetrajña iti kalpitaḥ sa hi sarvagataś caiva nirguṇaś caiva kathyate
english: But the goal of the liberated, O brāhmaṇa, is conceived as the Knower of the Field; for he is declared to be all-pervading and devoid of attributes.

sanskrit: dṛśyate jñānayogena āvāṃ ca prasṛtau tataḥ evaṃ jñātvā tam ātmānaṃ pūjayāvaḥ sanātanam
english: He is seen through the discipline of knowledge, and from him we two have issued forth; so, having known that Self, we worship the Eternal.

sanskrit: taṃ vedāś cāśramāś caiva nānātanusamāsthitāḥ bhaktyā saṃpūjayanty ādyaṃ gatiṃ caiṣāṃ dadāti saḥ
english: Him the Vedas and the orders of life, abiding in their manifold forms, worship with devotion as the Primeval One, and he grants them their goal.

sanskrit: ye tu tadbhāvitā loke ekāntitvaṃ samāsthitāḥ etad abhyadhikaṃ teṣāṃ yat te taṃ praviśanty uta
english: But those who, filled with the thought of That, have taken their stand in single-minded devotion — this is the surpassing portion of theirs: that they indeed enter into Him.

sanskrit: iti guhyasamuddeśas tava nārada kīrtitaḥ bhaktyā premṇā ca viprarṣe asmadbhaktyā ca te śrutaḥ
english: Thus the exposition of the mystery has been declared to you, Nārada; through devotion and love, O sage among brāhmaṇas, and through your devotion to us, you have heard it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa evam ukto dvipadāṃ variṣṭho; nārāyaṇenottamapūruṣeṇa jagāda vākyaṃ dvipadāṃ variṣṭhaṃ; nārāyaṇaṃ lokahitādhivāsam
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person, that noblest of two-footed beings spoke this word to Nārāyaṇa, the noblest of two-footed beings, the dwelling-place of the welfare of the worlds:

sanskrit: yadartham ātmaprabhaveha janma; tavottamaṃ dharmagṛhe caturdhā tat sādhyatāṃ lokahitārtham adya; gacchāmi draṣṭuṃ prakṛtiṃ tavādyām
english: For whatever purpose, O self-originated one, your supreme fourfold birth has come to be here in the house of Dharma — let that be accomplished today for the good of the worlds. I go to behold your primal Nature.

sanskrit: vedāḥ svadhītā mama lokanātha; taptaṃ tapo nānṛtam uktapūrvam pūjāṃ gurūṇāṃ satataṃ karomi; parasya guhyaṃ na ca bhinnapūrvam
english: The Vedas I have well studied, O Lord of the worlds; austerity I have practised; never before have I spoken falsehood; I render worship to my teachers without ceasing, and never before have I betrayed another's secret.

sanskrit: guptāni catvāri yathāgamaṃ me; śatrau ca mitre ca samo 'smi nityam taṃ cādidevaṃ satataṃ prapanna; ekāntabhāvena vṛṇomy ajasram ebhir viśeṣaiḥ pariśuddhasattvaḥ; kasmān na paśyeyam anantam īśam
english: The four are guarded by me according to scripture; toward foe and friend I am ever the same; taking refuge unceasingly in that Primal God, I choose Him without ceasing in single-minded spirit. With my being made wholly pure by these excellences, why should I not behold the infinite Lord?

sanskrit: tat pārameṣṭhyasya vaco niśamya; nārāyaṇaḥ sātvatadharmagoptā gaccheti taṃ nāradam uktavān sa; saṃpūjayitvātmavidhikriyābhiḥ
english: Hearing that word of the son of the Supreme One, Nārāyaṇa, the guardian of the Sātvata law, having honoured Nārada with the rites prescribed for himself, said to him, "Go."

sanskrit: tato visṛṣṭaḥ parameṣṭhiputraḥ; so 'bhyarcayitvā tam ṛṣiṃ purāṇam kham utpapātottamavegayuktas; tato 'dhimerau sahasā nililye
english: Then, dismissed, the son of the Supreme One, having reverenced that ancient seer, sprang up into the sky with the highest speed, and thereupon swiftly came to rest upon Meru's height.

sanskrit: tatrāvatasthe ca munir muhūrtam; ekāntam āsādya gireḥ sa śṛṅge ālokayann uttarapaścimena; dadarśa cātyadbhutarūpayuktam
english: And there the sage halted for a moment, having gained a solitary spot upon the mountain's peak; gazing toward the northwest, he beheld a region endowed with a most wondrous form.

sanskrit: kṣīrodadher uttarato hi dvīpaḥ; śvetaḥ sa nāmnā prathito viśālaḥ meroḥ sahasraiḥ sa hi yojanānāṃ; dvātriṃśatordhvaṃ kavibhir niruktaḥ
english: To the north of the Ocean of Milk lies an island, vast, renowned by the name of Śveta, the White; thirty-two thousand leagues beyond Meru it is reckoned by the wise.

sanskrit: atīndriyāś cānaśanāś ca tatra; niṣpandahīnāḥ susugandhinaś ca śvetāḥ pumāṃso gatasarvapāpāś; cakṣurmuṣaḥ pāpakṛtāṃ narāṇām
english: There the men are beyond the senses, without need of food, free of all motionlessness, and most fragrant — white men, with all sin departed, who rob the very sight of evil-doing men.

sanskrit: vajrāsthikāyāḥ samamānonmānā; divyānvayarūpāḥ śubhasāropetāḥ chatrākṛtiśīrṣā meghaughaninādāḥ; satpuṣkaracatuṣkā rājīvaśatapādāḥ
english: Their bodies are of adamantine bone, equal in measure and proportion, of celestial lineage and form, endowed with auspicious strength; their heads shaped like parasols, their voices like a mass of thunderclouds, with four fair lotus-marks, and a hundred lotuses upon their feet.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭyā dantair yuktāḥ śuklair; aṣṭābhir daṃṣṭrābhir ye jihvābhir ye viṣvagvaktraṃ; lelihyante sūryaprakhyam
english: Furnished with sixty white teeth and with eight tusks, they are such as lick on every side, with their tongues, a face that shines like the sun.

sanskrit: bhaktyā devaṃ viśvotpannaṃ; yasmāt sarve lokāḥ sūtāḥ vedā dharmā munayaḥ śāntā; devāḥ sarve tasya visargāḥ
english: With devotion they worship the god, the source of all, from whom all the worlds are brought forth; the Vedas, the laws, the tranquil sages, and all the gods are his emanations.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atīndriyā nirāhārā aniṣpandāḥ sugandhinaḥ kathaṃ te puruṣā jātāḥ kā teṣāṃ gatir uttamā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Beyond the senses, without food, unmoving, fragrant — how were these men born, and what is their highest goal?

sanskrit: ye vimuktā bhavantīha narā bharatasattama teṣāṃ lakṣaṇam etad dhi yac chvetadvīpavāsinām
english: This indeed is the mark of those men who become liberated here, O best of the Bharatas — the mark of the dwellers of Śvetadvīpa.

sanskrit: tasmān me saṃśayaṃ chindhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me tvaṃ hi sarvakathārāmas tvāṃ caivopāśritā vayam
english: Therefore cut away my doubt, for great is my curiosity; for you are the pleasure-garden of all tales, and upon you we have taken our stand.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vistīrṇaiṣā kathā rājañ śrutā me pitṛsaṃnidhau saiṣā tava hi vaktavyā kathāsāro hi sa smṛtaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: This is a far-reaching tale, O king, heard by me in my father's presence; and it must be told to you, for it is remembered as the very essence of narratives.

sanskrit: rājoparicaro nāma babhūvādhipatir bhuvaḥ ākhaṇḍalasakhaḥ khyāto bhakto nārāyaṇaṃ harim
english: There was a sovereign of the earth named Uparicara, a renowned friend of Indra the Cleaver, devoted to Nārāyaṇa Hari.

sanskrit: dhārmiko nityabhaktaś ca pitṝn nityam atandritaḥ sāmrājyaṃ tena saṃprāptaṃ nārāyaṇavarāt purā
english: Righteous, ever devout, and unwearied in his constant service to the fathers, he had obtained imperial sway of old through a boon of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: sātvataṃ vidhim āsthāya prāk sūryamukhaniḥsṛtam pūjayām āsa deveśaṃ taccheṣeṇa pitāmahān
english: Following the Sātvata rite, which issued forth of old from the mouth of the Sun, he worshipped the Lord of the gods, and with the remnant of that worship he honoured his forefathers.

sanskrit: pitṛśeṣeṇa viprāṃś ca saṃvibhajyāśritāṃś ca saḥ śeṣānnabhuk satyaparaḥ sarvabhūteṣv ahiṃsakaḥ sarvabhāvena bhaktaḥ sa devadevaṃ janārdanam
english: And with what remained from the fathers he shared among the brāhmaṇas and among his dependants; eating only the leavings, devoted to truth, harming no creature, he worshipped with his whole being the God of gods, Janārdana.

sanskrit: tasya nārāyaṇe bhaktiṃ vahato 'mitrakarśana ekaśayyāsanaṃ śakro dattavān devarāṭ svayam
english: As he bore this devotion to Nārāyaṇa, O harrier of foes, Śakra the king of the gods himself granted him a shared couch and seat.

sanskrit: ātmā rājyaṃ dhanaṃ caiva kalatraṃ vāhanāni ca etad bhagavate sarvam iti tat prekṣitaṃ sadā
english: Himself, his kingdom and his wealth, his wife and his mounts — all this is the blessed Lord's: thus was it ever regarded by him.

sanskrit: kāmyanaimittikājasraṃ yajñiyāḥ paramakriyāḥ sarvāḥ sātvatam āsthāya vidhiṃ cakre samāhitaḥ
english: The voluntary, the occasional, and the perpetual sacrificial acts, the highest rites — all of them he performed with collected mind, following the Sātvata ordinance.

sanskrit: pañcarātravido mukhyās tasya gehe mahātmanaḥ prāyaṇaṃ bhagavatproktaṃ bhuñjate cāgrabhojanam
english: The foremost knowers of the Pañcarātra in the house of that great-souled king observed the discipline taught by the Lord and partook of the first-offered food.

sanskrit: tasya praśāsato rājyaṃ dharmeṇāmitraghātinaḥ nānṛtā vāk samabhavan mano duṣṭaṃ na cābhavat na ca kāyena kṛtavān sa pāpaṃ param aṇv api
english: While that slayer of foes ruled his kingdom by righteousness, no false word arose from him, nor did his mind grow corrupt, nor did he commit by his body any sin, not even the most minute.

sanskrit: ye hi te munayaḥ khyātāḥ sapta citraśikhaṇḍinaḥ tair ekamatibhir bhūtvā yat proktaṃ śāstram uttamam
english: Those seven sages renowned as the Citraśikhaṇḍins — being of one mind, they proclaimed the supreme scripture.

sanskrit: marīcir atryaṅgirasau pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ vasiṣṭhaś ca mahātejā ete citraśikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: Marīci, Atri, and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha of great splendour — these are the Citraśikhaṇḍins.

sanskrit: sapta prakṛtayo hy etās tathā svāyaṃbhuvo 'ṣṭamaḥ etābhir dhāryate lokas tābhyaḥ śāstraṃ viniḥsṛtam
english: These are the seven primary principles, and Svāyaṃbhuva is the eighth; by these the world is upheld, and from them the scripture has issued forth.

sanskrit: ekāgramanaso dāntā munayaḥ saṃyame ratāḥ idaṃ śreya idaṃ brahma idaṃ hitam anuttamam lokān saṃcintya manasā tataḥ śāstraṃ pracakrire
english: Single-minded, self-controlled, the sages delighting in restraint — "This is the good, this is the Absolute, this is the highest welfare" — pondering the worlds in their minds, they then composed the scripture.

sanskrit: tatra dharmārthakāmā hi mokṣaḥ paścāc ca kīrtitaḥ maryādā vividhāś caiva divi bhūmau ca saṃsthitāḥ
english: Therein righteousness, gain, and desire, and liberation thereafter, are proclaimed; and manifold bounds besides, established in heaven and upon earth.

sanskrit: ārādhya tapasā devaṃ hariṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ vai sarve te ṛṣibhiḥ saha
english: Having propitiated by austerity the god Hari Nārāyaṇa, the Lord, for a thousand celestial years, all of them together with the seers —

sanskrit: nārāyaṇānuśāstā hi tadā devī sarasvatī viveśa tān ṛṣīn sarvāṃl lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: then the goddess Sarasvatī, instructed by Nārāyaṇa, entered into all those seers, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.
